papers.title: Sustained Activation of a Defensive Behavior-Related Circuit Elicits a distinct Homeostatic Sleep Response
papers.summary: The study compared homeostatic sleep responses after sustained wakefulness induced by gentle handling (GH) versus optogenetic activation of basal forebrain vGluT2 neurons in mice. vGluT2 stimulation produced a smaller increase in NREM sleep time and delta power during recovery than GH, and stronger cFos activity in stress and defensive behavior regions, indicating a distinct and diminished homeostatic sleep response.

papers.title: SSSI: A simulation-based framework for evaluating sigma-power fluctuation state identification pipelines in NREM sleep EEG.
papers.summary: The paper presents SSSI, a simulation-based framework for evaluating pipelines that identify sigma-power fluctuation (SPF) states in NREM sleep EEG. Applying this framework to mouse NREM and human N2 sleep revealed within-episode changes in SPF-state proportions, with age-dependent variation in humans, and showed that detected effects can depend on the analysis pipeline.

papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models
papers.summary: The paper presents Somnus, an open-source Python package for automated rodent sleep staging using EEG, EMG, and optional video data, trained on recordings from six laboratories. Somnus allows rapid adaptation to pathological sleep through a graphical interface that targets uncertain epochs for manual correction, enabling accurate custom scorers for disease models with minimal manual effort.

papers.title: Irreversible functional network deformation induced by preprocessing scheme order in multivariate EEG recordings.
papers.summary: The study quantitatively compared two EEG preprocessing schemes differing in the order of filtering and re-referencing, using sleep recordings, synthetic models, and surrogate testing. It found that re-referencing before filtering induces spurious cross-correlations that increase with frequency band and become irreversible for steep-spectrum signals (beta >= 2), while filtering before re-referencing introduces only small, correctable shifts.

papers.title: Sleep-dependent modulation of thalamic brain temperature estimates in humans
papers.summary: The study validated metabolite-cycled MRS for non-invasive brain temperature estimation and re-analyzed thalamic MRS data from young adults who slept in the scanner. NREM sleep entry reduced estimated thalamic temperature by 0.2 degrees Celsius, with deeper NREM sleep associated with greater decreases, suggesting an evening nap lowers thalamic temperature.

papers.title: Hyperglycaemia reversibly disrupts circadian behaviour in mice
papers.summary: Using an inducible mouse model of diabetes, the study showed that hyperglycaemia reversibly reduced the amplitude of circadian rest-activity rhythms by 50%, shortened the free-running period, delayed activity onset, and slowed re-entrainment after simulated jet lag. Restoring normoglycaemia reversed these effects, and brain glucose and O-GlcNAcylation were elevated, linking peripheral hyperglycaemia to altered brain metabolic state.

papers.title: What EEG doesn't see: a whole-brain MEG map of sleep spindles and slow oscillations
papers.summary: Using simultaneous MEG-EEG in 19 adults during a nap, the authors mapped the whole-brain amplitude and density of sleep spindles and slow oscillations across 416 cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions and compared them with a single scalp derivation (Cz-M1). Both rhythms were detected throughout the brain, with regional differences in spindle subtype and SO frequency balance, and scalp Cz-M1 provided a selective and partly composite view of sleep oscillations.

papers.title: Intersectional genetic targeting of molecularly distinct melanin-concentrating hormone neuron subpopulations reveals distinct and overlapping subcircuit architecture
papers.summary: The study used single-cell transcriptomics to identify Tacr3 and Cartpt as markers of at least two molecularly distinct MCH neuron subpopulations in the lateral hypothalamic area. By developing intersectional genetic tools, including a Tacr3-Flpo line and ConVERGD targeting, it mapped overlapping and distinct axonal projections of Type I (Pmch+/Tacr3+) and Type II (Pmch+/Tacr3-) MCH neurons, establishing a subpopulation-resolved anatomical framework.

papers.title: Distinct electroencephalography alpha-band rhythms map macroscale brain gradients.
papers.summary: Source-reconstructed resting-state EEG from 608 adults revealed that parcel-wise alpha peak frequencies were often bimodal, with two separable alpha-frequency components in 38.3% of recordings. Low-dimensional analysis identified two principal axes, including a sensorimotor–association axis resembling established functional-connectomic gradients, suggesting that split alpha reflects sensory-anchored oscillatory modes embedded in macroscale cortical organization.

papers.title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers.
papers.summary: In 2-3 year olds, a ~90-min nap versus wake after familiarization with two spatial contexts enhanced context memory and toy-context associations, and contextual memory correlated positively with NREM spindle density and slow oscillation-spindle phase-amplitude coupling.

papers.title: Protective role of high-intensity exercise and lactate against sleep deprivation-induced alterations in hippocampal gene expression and spatial learning.
papers.summary: Tested the protective effects of six weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and lactate administration against 48-hour sleep deprivation in rats, assessing spatial learning via Morris Water Maze and hippocampal gene expression of PKA, LIMK, and cofilin. Sleep deprivation downregulated memory-related genes, but both HIIT and lactate reversed these impairments, notably increasing LIMK expression, despite no significant differences in spatial learning performance across groups.

papers.title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: The authors developed an automated, interpretable pipeline using a single hour of ICU cEEG to estimate near-term seizure risk, combining automated interictal-ictal continuum probabilities with quantitative background EEG features. In 50 adults, the combined-feature SVM achieved 76% accuracy at the 4-hour horizon (Brier score 0.25), with accuracy declining from 94% at 1 hour to 79% at 24 hours; initial external validation supported generalizability.

papers.title: Event-Weighted Desaturation Burden and Cardiovascular Mortality in Sleep Apnoea: Findings from a Large Community-Based Prospective Cohort.
papers.summary: Developed event-weighted desaturation burden (EWDB), a composite metric integrating weighted respiratory event load, inter-event interval regularity, and cumulative desaturation area, and evaluated its association with cardiovascular mortality in 4,904 adults from the Sleep Heart Health Study. Higher EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality and provided incremental prognostic value beyond AHI and hypoxic burden, whereas AHI and HB lost significance after full adjustment.

papers.title: Circadian Timekeeping in the Tropics: Rhythmic Transcriptome and Diurnal Regulatory Networks in Rubroshorea leprosula.
papers.summary: Generated a circadian transcriptome of Rubroshorea leprosula, a dominant tropical rainforest tree, by sampling one sapling every 4 hours over 48 hours in constant darkness. Found that only ~1.3% of expressed genes were rhythmically expressed, with periods concentrated at 23–25 hours, and identified conserved orthologs of Arabidopsis core clock genes with similar phase timing but reduced amplitudes and lower coefficients of variation.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythms in Drug Response: From Molecular Clocks to Precision Dosing.
papers.journal: Annual review of pharmacology and toxicology
papers.summary: This review evaluates emerging research on circadian regulation of drug responses, covering both pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, and discusses chronotherapeutic strategies for cancer, cardiovascular disease, and bipolar disorder. It also addresses wearable technologies for time-resolved drug evaluation and challenges to integrating circadian timing into precision medicine and optimized dosing.

papers.title: Time-of-Day Variation in Knee Extensor Strength and Fatigue Is Associated With Circadian Phenotype in Healthy Young Adults.
papers.summary: Examined time-of-day variation in knee extensor strength and fatigue in 44 healthy young adults using a randomized crossover design with morning and evening testing, plus actigraphy and chronotype assessment. Found that maximal voluntary isometric contraction torque, fatigue resistance, contractions completed, and time-to-exhaustion were all greater in the evening, and chronotype explained 47% of the variance in diurnal performance difference.

papers.title: Effects of General Anaesthesia on the Sleep Structure of Patients With Prolonged Disorders of Consciousness.
papers.summary: This prospective study compared pre- and postoperative polysomnography in 30 patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness undergoing spinal cord stimulation under general anaesthesia, finding impaired baseline sleep structure versus controls and that anaesthesia prolonged total sleep time without significant changes in sleep-stage percentages or CRS-R scores.

papers.title: An Explainable Self-Supervised Temporal Transformer for Participant-Level Classification of Depressive Symptoms From Resting-State EEG.
papers.journal: International journal of methods in psychiatric research
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable self-supervised temporal transformer for participant-level classification of BDI-defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting-state EEG, reporting an ROC-AUC of 0.82 with SHAP and attention-based attribution while cautioning that findings do not establish clinical diagnostic validity or external generalizability.

papers.title: Effects of morning versus evening high-intensity exercise on electroencephalographic and autonomic responses in middle-aged women.
papers.summary: Compared EEG and autonomic responses to morning versus evening high-intensity exercise in 30 middle-aged women, measuring theta-to-beta ratio (TBR), spectral edge frequency at 90% (SEF-90), and HRV indices. Found significant group × time interactions, with greater pre- to post-exercise changes in TBR, SEF-90, and HRV-derived sympathetic and parasympathetic indices in the morning group.

papers.title: Impact of environmental enrichment and allostatic load induced by repeated mixing on the transcriptome of three porcine brain tissues.
papers.summary: RNA sequencing of hypothalamus, prefrontal cortex, and hippocampus from 48 gilts in a 2x2 enrichment and repeated-mixing design found that allostatic load induced 38 differentially expressed genes in hippocampus, whereas environmental enrichment had minimal transcriptomic impact.

papers.title: Vascular brain injury modifies the relationship between sleep duration, cognition, and white matter hyperintensity burden in the Alzheimer's disease continuum.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: In a deeply phenotyped cohort of 735 individuals across the Alzheimer's disease continuum, vascular brain injury (WMH+ status) significantly amplified the association between shorter sleep duration and greater white matter hyperintensity burden in MCI+V and AD groups; in AD, longer sleep related to better cognition in WMH+ but worse cognition in WMH-only.

papers.title: The link between inflammation and autonomic dysfunction in alpha-synucleinopathies - narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the link between inflammation and autonomic dysfunction in alpha-synucleinopathies, highlighting that elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IFN-α) accompany dysautonomic symptoms and that immunomodulatory approaches, including intravenous immunoglobulin, dietary modification, probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation, are potential therapeutic strategies requiring further research.

papers.title: Cardiac fibrosis and heart failure: Metabolic stress, circadian dysregulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling.
papers.summary: This review examines how circadian rhythm disruption, particularly from artificial light at night, exacerbates diabetic cardiac fibrosis. It proposes that loss of circadian regulation amplifies TGF-β signaling, Rho-A/ROCK mechanotransduction, and oxidative stress, highlighting chronotherapeutic strategies to reduce heart failure risk.

papers.title: Migration Characteristics and Mechanism of Active Components From Jieyu Anshen Granule in Different Insomnia Mouse Models.
papers.journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM
papers.summary: Using PCPA- and sleep-deprivation-induced insomnia mouse models, this study identified 89 in vitro and 43 blood-absorbed components of Jieyu Anshen Granule with tissue-specific distribution and predicted furanogermenone and curcumenol as core anti-insomnia components targeting ADORA2A, GABRB3, and SLC6A4.

papers.title: Ligustilide enhances TNTs-mediated mitochondrial transfer to accelerate the reactivation of TECs in sleep deprivation induced postpartum mouse.
papers.summary: In postpartum mice with sleep deprivation, ligustilide (1 mg/kg) restored thymic epithelial cell (TEC) localization and thymocyte development, increasing CD4+ T-cell output. Mechanistically, ligustilide promoted F-actin-dependent tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) between thymocytes and TECs, mediating mitochondrial transfer via Rho GTPase (Cdc42) signaling.

papers.title: Cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation in pediatric epileptic syndromes: mechanisms, limitations, and future research horizons.
papers.summary: This review evaluates cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation (c-tDCS) for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy, reporting from meta-analyses a significant reduction in seizure frequency (about 45% at 4 weeks) and favorable safety from over 600 sessions. It highlights mechanisms, limitations, and future research priorities including closed-loop stimulation and biomarker-driven selection.

papers.title: Real-time wearable detection of respiratory infections in pediatric transplant households
papers.summary: Deploys a resting heart rate-based real-time alerting algorithm from consumer wearables to detect respiratory infections in pediatric transplant households (n=146) within a Phase IV clinical trial. Of 31 antigen-test outcomes, 29 (93.5%) corresponded to influenza, COVID, or patient-reported symptoms, and the authors describe heart rate, activity, and sleep/circadian features around alarm events as candidate signals for algorithm improvement.

papers.title: Attenuated attention engagement and sensorimotor resonance to social events in first-episode adolescent depression: Evidence from EEG oscillations.
papers.summary: EEG was recorded in first-episode adolescent depression and healthy controls during observation of social interactions. Depressed adolescents showed no differential mu suppression for giving vs. disposing events and higher occipital alpha power for social versus non-social targets, with attenuated sensorimotor resonance correlating with symptom severity.

papers.title: The Association of Window Ventilation Frequency with Depressive Symptoms Among Older Chinese People: Perceived Sleep Duration and Psychological Resilience.
papers.summary: In 11,374 Chinese adults aged ≥65 from CLHLS 2018, higher window ventilation frequency was negatively associated with depressive symptoms, with strongest mitigation in spring and weakest in winter. Serial mediation showed significant indirect pathways via self-reported total sleep duration and psychological resilience, both separately and sequentially.

papers.title: [Tiaoshen acupuncture for shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder: a randomized controlled trial].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
keywords: Shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial with 84 shift workers, Tiaoshen acupuncture improved sleep-wake rhythm (MEQ) and sleep quality (PSQI) and reduced anxiety and depression scores compared to non-acupoint needling. Benefits persisted for sleep quality at 3 months.

papers.title: Shift work and hormonal-circadian disruption raise urinary incontinence: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence linking circadian rhythm disruption and hormonal imbalance to pelvic floor dysfunction and urinary incontinence, emphasizing night-shift work as a model of chronic chronobiological stress. It proposes integrated neuroimmunoendocrine mechanisms involving melatonin suppression, cortisol dysregulation, and inflammation, and outlines preventive approaches including pelvic floor physiotherapy, sleep hygiene, schedule correction, and local estrogen therapy.

papers.title: AcNR1F orchestrates epidermal remodeling to enable host adaptation in Angiostrongylus cantonensis.
papers.summary: Characterizes the nuclear receptor AcNR1F in Angiostrongylus cantonensis, showing it is a ligand-activated receptor that regulates development, reproduction, and epidermal integrity. RNAi knockdown reduced adult recovery and egg production by 64%, caused abnormal eggs with low hatching, and produced a thinned cuticle; col-12 and col-144 were direct AcNR1F targets, and host-derived cholesterol, corticosterone, and 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol acted as ligands, implicating AcNR1F in host adaptation.

papers.title: Sustained Seizure Freedom After Stereo-Electroencephalography Without Definitive Intervention: Evidence for Network Modulation by Invasive EEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Two patients with drug-resistant epilepsy achieved sustained seizure freedom after stereo-EEG monitoring without resection or neuromodulation, remaining seizure-free for 71 and 20 months. The cases suggest that sEEG implantation may induce microlesional or network-modulatory effects capable of interrupting seizure propagation.

papers.title: From localized to long-range: functional connectivity alterations in mild to moderate chronic low back pain patients.
papers.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
papers.summary: Comparing 55 mild-to-moderate chronic low back pain patients with 39 healthy controls using static/dynamic ReHo and seed-based resting-state fMRI, the study found reduced sReHo in cerebellar vermis III, reduced dReHo in right parahippocampal gyrus and left inferior temporal gyrus, and altered long-range connectivity in cerebello-hippocampal and cortico-basal ganglia pathways. These neurofunctional changes correlated with anxiety and McGill Pain Questionnaire scores, suggesting early central alterations in low-intensity chronic pain.

papers.title: An Exploratory Retrospective Comparison of Crisugabalin and Pregabalin Among 12-Week Treatment Completers With Postherpetic Neuralgia.
papers.summary: This single-center retrospective cohort of 113 postherpetic neuralgia patients completing ≥12 weeks of monotherapy compared crisugabalin (n=56) and pregabalin (n=57) using linear mixed models. Crisugabalin showed greater improvements over time on NRS, PSQI, and SF-36 mental component scores, with no significant overall difference in adverse events, though authors note exploratory and bias-prone findings requiring prospective confirmation.

papers.title: The Neural Symphony in the Periodontium: Health, Inflammation, and Regeneration.
papers.summary: This review characterizes the spatiotemporal plasticity of periodontal nerves and dissects molecular mechanisms linking neural signaling to periodontal immunity, bone remodeling, and repair. It highlights that neural equilibrium (e.g., CGRP and acetylcholine versus substance P and catecholamines) is required for periodontal regeneration and proposes nerve-targeted strategies including neurotrophin-functionalized biomaterials, local neuropeptide delivery, and bioelectric neuromodulation.

papers.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Multiple Sclerosis: A Topical Narrative Review.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: This narrative review addresses the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists in people with multiple sclerosis, covering weight loss in comorbid obesity, efficacy for approved non-MS indications such as diabetes and obstructive sleep apnea, and potential pleiotropic effects on MS disease course beyond approved indications.

papers.title: Acute Onset Orolingual Choreoathetosis and Auditory Hallucinations in a Healthy Young Adult Following High Melatonin Dose.
papers.summary: A healthy 22-year-old man developed acute orolingual choreoathetosis and auditory hallucinations after ingesting 132 mg of melatonin following three nights of 24 mg. Symptoms resolved within 24 hours, but confounders included sleep deprivation and heat exposure; causality remains unestablished.

papers.title: Virtual reality as a metacognitive training tool for lucid dreaming.
papers.summary: This 5-week study tested whether a virtual reality intervention rehearsing lucid-dream-relevant metacognitive routines increases lucid dreaming rates beyond standard training or generic VR exposure. VR-experimental participants reported the highest number of lucid-like dreams (26) versus Control (11) and VR-control (4), with significantly higher rates than VR-control (RR = 8.60) and Control (RR = 4.00), indicating that dream-oriented VR training preceded by open-monitoring meditation may scaffold metacognitive monitoring from wakefulness to REM sleep.

papers.title: Predictors of Activity and Concentration Interference in Adults with Migraine: An Ecological Momentary Assessment Study
papers.summary: This prospective ecological momentary assessment study of 143 adults with migraine used cumulative link mixed-effects models to identify daily predictors of headache-related interference with activity and concentration. Brain fog, forgetfulness, and mood disturbance were independently associated with both outcomes, while sleep quality and anticipated next-day enjoyment explained additional variance only for activity interference, showing that cognitive and affective symptoms rather than demographic factors are primary correlates.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
